paragraphs: Rav Shmuel, son of Rabbah bar bar Chana.

He was Rabbah’s student. Shevuot 36b relates that he, Rav Acha bar Huna and Rav Yitzchak son of Rav Yehudah were studying Shevuot in Rabbah’s school. Rav Kahana met them; Rava bar Itai said to them, etc. In Kiddushin 58a Mar Yehudah found Rav Yosef and Rav Shmuel son of Rabbah bar bar Chana at Rabbah’s doorway and questioned them. They could not answer. When they came to Rabbah, he told them: “Someone who disputes my views has confronted you.” Hyman considers it very likely that he is also called Rav Shmuel bar bar Chana, who objects to Rav Yosef in Shabbat 29a. In 59b and 146b he tells Rav Yosef, “You explicitly told us in Rav’s name,” etc.

notes.text: Rav Kahana is explicitly named in Shevuot. The parenthetical criticism in Kiddushin describes an opponent challenging Rabbah’s students, not making them “half-men.” Hyman’s longer and shorter Shmuel patronymics remain separate forms.

The consulted Shevuot 36b ends after Kahana met the students; 37a continues his question and the students’ reply, then explicitly names Rava bar Itai. Kiddushin 58a names Yosef and Shmuel at Rabbah’s doorway and gives Rabbah’s opponent remark. Hyman’s very-likely equation of the longer and shorter Shmuel patronymics remains his inference, not identity admission.
